USMLE-style practice · Clinical medicine

Recurrence and definitive assessment

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 21-year-old has recovered from his third documented peritonsillar abscess in two years. He also reports multiple episodes of disabling tonsillitis. He is currently well with no acute obstruction. What is the most appropriate next step?

  1. ENT assessment for possible tonsillectomy
  2. Long-term suppressive antibiotics as the sole plan
  3. Routine imaging surveillance without surgical review
  4. No further assessment unless airway obstruction develops
  5. Immediate abscess drainage while asymptomatic
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

ENT assessment for possible tonsillectomy

Recurrent quinsy and significant tonsillitis justify discussion of tonsillectomy after individualized assessment.

Understanding the options

ENT assessment for possible tonsillectomy
Recurrent quinsy and significant tonsillitis justify discussion of tonsillectomy after individualized assessment.
Long-term suppressive antibiotics as the sole plan
Indefinite suppression does not substitute for evaluation of recurrent abscesses and disabling tonsillitis.
Routine imaging surveillance without surgical review
Recurrent episodes justify individualized ENT discussion rather than imaging alone.
No further assessment unless airway obstruction develops
Waiting for obstruction overlooks the morbidity of recurrent quinsy and the potential role of elective surgery.
Immediate abscess drainage while asymptomatic
There is no current collection to drain; the question concerns prevention after recovery.
